blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: A multimodal agent must decide whether visual evidence is worth acquiring, which candidate or resolution to query, and when further interaction can no longer change its decision. We study this problem under a strict free-metadata/paid-observation boundary, stochastic vector costs, and a frozen execution trace, and treat it as decision-certifiable active evidence acquisition. A Counterfactual Evidence Interaction Graph (CEIG) represents unary evidence value, signed second-order interaction, and directed conditional harm while maintaining explicit score enclosures for unresolved interactions; a decision-weighted enclosure objective tightens the bounds that can change action identity. Gap-directed refinement evaluates only interactions that can displace the incumbent acquisition and stops once an $ε$-decision certificate shows that unresolved terms cannot change the selected action beyond a declared tolerance. The certificate is model-relative: it verifies policy-consistent optimality under the pinned learned score, and semantic quality is measured separately through post-freeze labels. Paired continuation rollouts learn the downstream value of paid previews, an online operational cost filter is separated from independent finite-policy-family trajectory certification, and an acquisition monitor with an independently implemented verifier binds every certificate to the frozen trace. On 640 cases split into 384/128/128 training, validation, and test cases, the controller reaches task score 0.842, grounding F1 0.816, evidence recall 0.873, 1.74 accepted calls, 286.5K visual tokens, and 742ms p95 latency. Dense replay of issued certificates shows 0.992 action agreement and a 0.988 certificate rate while evaluating 19.6 instead of 191.4 expensive interaction terms per decision.

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 导言

blocks.en:
A multimodal agent receives a user request, a candidate pool of visual
evidence served through a metered acquisition interface, and an explicit
resource budget. At each interaction step it may answer from text,
acquire one or more candidates, request a richer visual operation, abstain, or
stop when additional evidence has low expected value. Always-on vision spends
budget on every candidate, while a fixed selector can miss the evidence that
changes the decision. We study this as sequential evidence acquisition with an
information boundary: the online policy sees selection-time fields and the
acquired observations, while task labels and post-hoc usefulness labels enter
only after the trace is frozen.

blocks.en:
Adaptive acquisition leaves three agent-level questions open. Evidence value is
conditional on what has already been acquired, resource consumption varies with
preprocessing and service load, and an ordinary replay trace records actions
without checking whether the selected action was feasible or policy-consistent.
Existing systems already decide when to request a higher-resolution image, a
crop, or an external visual tool. ActiveEvidence targets a different question:
when has an agent computed enough of the evidence-interaction structure to
justify a particular acquisition decision? Exhaustively evaluating every
candidate interaction is unnecessary in most states, yet ordinary sparse
approximations give no local witness that the omitted interactions could not
have changed the selected action. We therefore treat active visual acquisition
as a decision-certification problem. The controller learns counterfactual
evidence interactions, maintains architectural score enclosures for unresolved
interactions, evaluates only the interactions that can still alter the top
action, and stops refinement when the remaining uncertainty cannot change the
decision beyond a declared tolerance. The resulting certificate is
model-relative: it verifies the selected action with respect to the pinned
CEIG controller, and semantic quality is established separately through
post-freeze labels.

blocks.en:
ReAct treats reasoning and acting as an interleaved trajectory so that external
observations can redirect a plan ( Yao et al., 2023 ) . Toolformer studies

systems motivate recording the action and feedback boundary; ActiveEvidence
isolates the lower-level question of whether to acquire a visual observation
at all, and records the candidate, cost, and stop event for replay.

blocks.en:
Computer-use and user-facing task suites make environment state, tool
contracts, and trace-level evaluation first-class ( Xie et al., 2024 ; Yao et al., 2025 ; Debenedetti et al., 2024 ) ; the decision
problem itself connects to value-of-information analysis ( Howard, 1966 ) , adaptive submodularity ( Golovin and Krause, 2011 ) , and constrained Markov decision processes ( Altman, 1999 ) . Agent metareasoning treats costly monitoring
and deliberation termination as decisions ( Carlin and Zilberstein, 2011 ) ;
Monte Carlo value-of-information planning evaluates evidence sequences
whose joint value can exceed individual contributions ( Kamar and Horvitz, 2013 ) .
Metareasoning evaluates computations by their downstream decision value ( Russell and Wefald, 1991 ; Hay et al., 2012 ) ; bounded-optimal agency and
anytime composition make computational limits explicit ( Russell and Subramanian, 1995 ; Zilberstein and Russell, 1996 ) . Nonmyopic information
value and cost-sensitive feature acquisition capture evidence complementarity ( Heckerman et al., 1993 ; Bilgic and Getoor, 2011 ) ; active perception and
information-reward planning treat sensing as an action ( Bajcsy, 1988 ; Spaan et al., 2015 ) . ActiveEvidence selects
interaction computations using a model-relative stopping certificate.

blocks.en: 3.1. Method Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1. 方法概述

blocks.en:
ActiveEvidence separates prediction, decision refinement, and execution
verification (Figure 1 ). At state s t s_{t} the online policy
observes only the request, the free candidate manifest, already paid preview
fields, acquired evidence, and the remaining resource vector. A Need Gate
predicts the value of another observation, the CEIG predicts unary evidence

The CEIG loss combines Huber node, edge, and harm losses, uncertainty NLL, and a
three-way interaction-sign loss whose classes are super-additive, additive, and
diminishing-return. Pools with at most n full n_{\mathrm{full}} nodes
enumerate all feasible pairs; larger pools retain L L uncertainty-aware
neighbors per node, reducing edge scoring from O ⁡ ( n i 2 ) O(n_{i}^{2}) to O ⁡ ( n i ​ L ) O(n_{i}L) .
The train/validation/test split is 384 / 128 / 128 384/128/128 , the learning rate is 3.0 × 10 − 4 3.0\times 10^{-4} , and three controller seeds are recorded. The held-out
interaction error, sign AUROC, and complementary-evidence recovery are

blocks.en:
The semantic evidence rests on 128 held-out cases from four domains with
three controller seeds, so every slice-level comparison carries its case
count and interval (Appendix D.13 ); the decision certificate

supervision for CEIG and paired preview targets

queries, so the method suits deployments with sustained query volume.

blocks.en:
ActiveEvidence is a decision-certifiable framework for resource-bounded
multimodal evidence acquisition: the CEIG separates unary value, second-order
interaction, directed harm, and semantic contradiction; certificate-oriented
training tightens decision-relevant enclosures; gap-directed refinement

blocks.en:
This study tests whether the decision-weighted enclosure objective improves
decision certification rather than only interaction prediction. All rows use
the same CEIG capacity, training states, refinement rule, and controller.
“Uniform tightness” penalizes every unresolved interval width equally,
whereas the decision-weighted row uses ℒ cert \mathcal{L}_{\rm cert} and
concentrates enclosure capacity on edges that belong to near-optimal actions.
Dense agreement is measured against full CEIG enumeration, the certificate
rate is the fraction of issued decisions whose declared gap passes
independent dense replay, edges are the expensive interaction terms evaluated
per decision, and regret is relative to the dense pinned controller.

将封闭能力集中在接近最佳行动的边缘。
以完整的CEIG计数、证书来衡量协议是否合理
比率是所发布决定中宣布的差数的一小部分
独立密集重播,边缘是评价的昂贵的交互术语
每个决定, 遗憾是相对于密集的固定控制器。
